Hi Simon / Lucy —

Thanks again for the call today — helpful to hear your platform goals and the residency constraints for EU data. Quick recap and proposed next steps:

Summary of needs (from our discussion)
- Must keep production data and logs for EU customers in EU region for at-rest residency and auditability.
- APAC expansion likely in Q1; latency in APAC matters for your support agents.
- Procurement timeline: expect initial decision by end of August; procurement and security review in parallel.

Options recap (high-level)
- Hosted API: regional endpoints (we can pin to eu-west) and regional data processing, fastest to onboard; best for rapid POC.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool in a selected region (EU) — predictable throughput and stronger isolation, supports higher TPS.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full customer-managed networking and private control plane — recommended for strict residency & regulatory control or if you require on-prem processing.

Open questions for you
1) Do you require a private control plane (VPC) or is region-limited hosted/dedicated acceptable for initial rollout?
2) Are there specific latency SLOs for APAC users we should budget against?
3) Who will lead the security questionnaire on your side (name/email)?

Simon / Lucy —

Looping in Neha (Security & Compliance) and Marcus (Solutions) to answer the technical bits — below is a short breakdown from our side and proposed mitigation paths.

Hosted API (recommended for fast POC)
- Regional endpoints: We offer region-specific endpoints (e.g., eu-west-1) where processing and storage of request bodies, logs, and model caches are restricted to the selected region.
- Controls: configurable retention windows, log export (S3-compatible), and key management integration (KMS). We can provide SOC2 artifacts and an export of our dataflow diagram (attached).
- Notes: Hosted gives fastest time-to-value but is a multitenant control plane; data residency is enforced at the processing and storage layer. Fallbacks: cross-region routing can be configured at the account level for DR but is opt-in (we can disable automatic cross-region fallback if you require strict residency).

Dedicated capacity (middle ground)
- Reserved GPU pools deployed into a chosen region (EU). Provides stronger tenant isolation, predictable throughput, and support-level SLA for latency and uptime.
- Lead time: typically 2-4 weeks to provision in a new region depending on capacity availability; we can prioritize for deals in procurement.

Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Full customer-managed network and private control plane; recommended if you must keep all control-plane metadata off Redwood-managed infrastructure or for regulatory mandates requiring on-prem processing.
- Tradeoffs: longest procurement & setup (4-8+ weeks), but max control and easiest path for strict compliance.

APAC latency considerations
- Hosted in EU to APAC: median latency to SG/SYD will typically be 200-350ms depending on network; Dedicated capacity in APAC region reduces tail latencies significantly.
- For your 250ms median target we recommend either: 1) start with Hosted EU for POC and monitor metrics, or 2) provision Dedicated APAC capacity on go-live. Marcus can run a quick sim for expected median/95th numbers given your traffic mix.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2-summary.pdf (SOC artifacts), draft_sow-hosted-vs-vpc.docx (pricing and scope), finsecure-network-primer.png (network sketch).
